title: Desk Reference — Final Month Base Fee Charge on an Independent Living Residency
content:
**Product:** Independent Living Residency Agreement. **Subject:** the base monthly service fee charge of the final, partly used month.

## When this applies

This entry belongs to a residency on which a notice of termination stands, when the resident or the resident's representative asks to settle the residency. The final month is the calendar month after the last month already billed, and its base fee charge covers the days from the first day of that month through the date the residency's monthly fees end (the fee end date). The charge is posted on the day the settlement is asked for.

## Business effect

Posting writes one base fee charge entry on the residency ledger, marked as a move-out proration, covering the days from the first day of the calendar month of the last day given through that last day, dated the day of posting, and raises the account balance owed by the amount. The new monthly fee charge then appears on the residency ledger with the days it covers.

## Invocation — `post_final_month_charge_713925f6`

**Owner and access.** Agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `post_final_month_charge_713925f6` and then calls it.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `independent_residency_id` | The reference number of the independent living residency agreement whose account is charged, read from the residency lookup for the customer | Text identifier |
| `service_to_date` | The last day the charge covers — the date the residency's monthly fees end; the charge runs from the first day of that calendar month | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `amount` | The charge amount | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt lists `independent_entry_id` (the reference number of the new charge entry), `billing_period` (the month charged, YYYY-MM), `service_from_date` and `service_to_date` (the first and last day covered, YYYY-MM-DD), `days_billed` (integer days covered, both ends included), `amount` (USD with 2 decimal places), `account_balance` (the balance owed after the charge, USD with 2 decimal places) and `status`, reading `final_month_charge_posted`.

## Contract questions

**Which days does the entry cover?** From the first day of the calendar month of `service_to_date` through `service_to_date`, both ends included; `days_billed` is that count.

**What billing period does the entry carry?** The month of `service_to_date`.

Hypothetical illustration: a call with `service_to_date` 2026-11-18 posts a charge for billing period 2026-11 covering 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-18, with `days_billed` 18.
